image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky brown water. The view is primarily dorsal, showcasing the heavily armored back, neck, and top of the head. The skin texture is extremely detailed, showing rough, bony scutes (osteoderms) covered in patches of dried mud or algae. The snout is visible at the bottom center, with nostrils clearly defined. The eyes are positioned dorsally but appear closed or obscured by the angle and lighting. The tail extends towards the top of the frame, fading into the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout shape is visible at the bottom of the frame; it tapers to a point consistent with a crocodilian V-shape rather than a U-shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the angle is directly from above; the side profile of the jawline and teeth is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct nostril holes are clearly visible at the anterior tip of the snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating and an elongated structure extending out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface exhibits distinct, raised rows of scutes running longitudinally down the spine and tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is earthy brown/grey, and the texture is visibly rough and granular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal view; the belly/ventral side is completely occluded by the body and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in this specific crop/angle; they are either underwater or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending upwards; it appears muscular and textured with scutes, consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

The end of the tail seems to dissolve into the water/background without a clear termination point or splash, suggesting a minor generation boundary issue.
